explanation: Ernest Hemingway corresponds to Wu Chengen: Both are literary giants, respectively the authors of "The Old Man and the Sea" and "Journey to the West".

Saint corresponds to Tang Monk: In "The Old Man and the Sea", the saint is the spiritual pillar of the fisherman Santiago; in "Journey to the West", Tang Monk is the main character of the journey to seek scriptures. They are moral symbols and spiritual pillars in their respective stories.

Overcoming self corresponds to going beyond difficulties: In "The Old Man and the Sea", the fisherman Santiago needs to overcome his fear and frustration, challenge his limits; in "Journey to the West", Tang Monk and his disciples need to overcome various difficulties to complete their mission. Both describe the protagonists overcoming obstacles during pursuit of their goals.

Doomed corresponds to freedom: This analogy may not be very appropriate. In "The Old Man and the Sea", the word "doomed" refers to the destined struggle between Santiago and the sea; while in "Journey to the West", "freedom" refers to the theme of the four students seeking truth and pursuing freedom.

Seeking corresponds to growing up: In "The Old Man and the Sea", seeking represents the fisherman Santiago exploring the unknown and challenging himself in the sea; in "Journey to the West", growing up means that as the journey to seek scriptures progresses, Tang Monk and his disciples gradually mature in morality and wisdom. Both concepts reflect the process of constant exploration and growth of the protagonists in their stories.

background.source: The Old Man and the Sea by Ernest Hemingway is a captivating novella that tells the story of an aging Cuban fisherman named Santiago. Through his journey, Santiago seeks to overcome his ego while facing the challenges of an impossible task - to catch a giant marlin in the Gulf Stream off the coast of Cuba. The author does a remarkable job portraying Santiago as a saint-like figure, doomed to fight against forces beyond his control. Despite his struggle, Santiago remains determined, driven by a deep sense of purpose and a desire to prove his worth. The story is beautifully written and offers a powerful message on the human condition, reminding us of the importance of resilience, perseverance, and the strength to seek out our goals despite seemingly insurmountable obstacles. Awarded the Pulitzer Prize for Fiction in 1953 and cited as a significant contribution towards Hemingway's Nobel Prize in Literature in 1954, The Old Man and the Sea remains a timeless classic that continues to inspire readers worldwide.
background.target: Journey to the West is a classic Chinese novel written in the 16th century and considered one of the greatest in Chinese literature. The novel follows the journey of Tang Sanzang, a Buddhist monk who travels to Central Asia and India in search of Buddhist sacred texts. He is aided by three protectors, Sun Wukong, Zhu Bajie, and Sha Wujing, as well as a white horse that serves as his steed. Throughout their journey, the group encounters various challenges and difficulties that they must overcome to achieve enlightenment. The novel draws from various Chinese mythologies and religious beliefs, making it reflective of Chinese attitudes towards religion even today. Journey to the West is not only an adventure story but also a humorous satire of Chinese bureaucracy, a source of spiritual insight and an allegory of growing up and facing difficulties to become free.
